policy_title: Build Four New Prisons and Expand Removals
stated: The Conservative Party will build four new prisons, completing the programme of 20,000 new prison places by 2030, by scrapping legacy EU rules and streamlining the planning system. They will also remove more Foreign National Offenders by increasing removals under the Early Removal Scheme and negotiating more Prisoner Transfer Agreements.

source.quote: We will build four new prisons, completing our programme of 20,000 new prison places by 2030. ...We will remove more Foreign National Offenders by increasing removals under the Early Removal Scheme and negotiating more Prisoner Transfer Agreements.

bearing_set.reason: Building prison places and expanding removal of foreign national offenders directly affects the justice system's capacity, sentencing effectiveness, and public safety outcomes.

Four new prisons represent substantial capital expenditure (individual prisons typically cost £300–500m+) plus ongoing operational costs; if unfunded or deficit-financed, this materially affects the debt path and funded-vs-borrowed spending balance.

membership_note: O5 is the primary designed-for bearing; O12 is the fiscal tradeoff — concrete mechanism (large capital + operational spend) and specific indicator (debt path/funded spending) both clear the non-negligible bar. O10 was considered but not included: the prisons expand capacity for court-sentenced offenders, not new general surveillance or coercive powers over the wider public. O9 was considered for due process around Early Removal Scheme but the scheme operates within existing statutory frameworks, making the bearing negligible at this level of policy detail.
